sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Packaging and starting the frontend
sections.what: Sets up a container that installs the frontend libraries, copies the project in, opens port 3000, and starts the development server so the frontend is reachable in a browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: to run the frontend in a repeatable way. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Changes to the package list need a fresh image build, since the library install step is cached by Docker.

summary: A recipe that packages the frontend into a container image using Node.js 20 and starts its development server on port 3000.
purpose: Lets the frontend run the same way on any machine that has Docker, without installing Node.js by hand.
why: Likely reason: to make the frontend easy to start alongside the backend. Reason for choosing the development server is not stated in the code.
how: Starts from a small Node.js 20 base image, sets the working folder, copies the package list and installs dependencies, copies the rest of the project, opens port 3000, then runs the dev command.
inputs: The project files in the frontend folder and the package list in frontend/package.json.
outputs: A container image that serves the frontend on port 3000 when started.
risks: The dev server is meant for development, not for real users. Copying everything with one broad copy step may also bring in local files that are not needed, since no ignore file is visible.
debug: If the container does not start, check the build output for failed installs and confirm the package list is valid. If the page does not load, confirm port 3000 is mapped and that the dev server printed a ready message.
